page: Amazon Web Services r8in.8xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance features an x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz with 16 physical cores and 32 dedicated vCPUs. It incorporates 480 MB of L3 cache alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory capacity is configured with 256 GB of high-speed 7 GHz DDR5 RAM, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. The instance includes no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage, and provides a 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile without included discrete GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations show competitive single-threaded and integer capabilities, with Geekbench single-core scores reaching the top 10% bracket (2239.0) and multi-core scores placing in the top 25% (18905.0). Text processing and image manipulation tests also rank in the top decile. In compression tasks, single-threaded gzip reaches 34.11 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieves 228.63 GB/sec, both in the upper quartile. While small-parameter language model processing benefits from AMX execution units, larger model text generation falls off significantly due to the absence of dedicated GPU hardware. Memory bandwidth sustains 175.35 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 77.63 GB/sec on writes.

The r8in.8xlarge offers solid resource density for RAM-heavy enterprise applications, backed by 50 Gbps network connectivity. The lack of integrated local NVMe storage means sustained disk I/O depends entirely on external block storage allocation. This configuration fits in-memory caching solutions like Redis, intermediate data-processing jobs, memory-intensive database platforms, high-throughput static web delivery, and enterprise transactional systems requiring large DDR5 memory working sets.
description: Amazon Web Services r8in.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Powered by a 3.9 GHz Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor, it delivers 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with a 480 MB L3 cache, AVX-512, and AMX acceleration. The server is equipped with 256 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU allocation. There is no integrated local storage, and the instance operates with zero GPUs while delivering a 50 Gbps baseline network capacity. Benchmarks reveal strong single-thread execution, placing in the top 10% on Geekbench single-core and text processing metrics, accompanied by robust data compression throughput. Given its 1:8 core-to-memory profile and high-bandwidth interconnect, the instance is engineered for memory-bound workloads such as large-scale in-memory databases, Redis deployments, enterprise analytics, and high-throughput static web serving.
